subject: Local-first agents strengthen hybrid execution thesis without changing sprint
body_md: Thesis: local-first agent execution is becoming commercially real enough that Nexus should model execution locality as a policy/economics variable, but this does not justify buying hardware or interrupting the current procurement closed-loop bottleneck. Evidence: Perplexity published Portable Computer on Aug. 25, describing Computer running on-device with remote capabilities used on demand; VentureBeat independently reports local execution starts on-device and asks permission before escalating a step to a frontier cloud model. NVIDIA separately launched Jetson Orin Nano 2 for H1 2027 with 2x predecessor inference performance and 40% lower power at equivalent performance, reinforcing the broader edge/local-compute direction. Conviction: +0.79 on hybrid local/cloud execution becoming a durable agent architecture; +0.31 that owned local hardware is economically optimal for Nova soon. Contradictions: local hardware can have poor utilization, weaker model quality, maintenance cost, and the user's current laptop is not an RTX/Jetson-class target. What would falsify this: controlled Nexus tasks show local-first routing raises total cost, human review, latency, or failure rate versus API-first execution after privacy/data-custody benefits are included. Recommendation: keep as R&D state only; finish the existing GSA/DHS Wayfinder→policy→ledger→Operations transition before implementing locality routing.
thesis: Hybrid local/cloud execution should be a Nexus routing policy dimension, not a hardware-purchase trigger.
what_would_falsify_this: Nexus benchmark shows API-first execution beats local-first on verified outcome cost and latency after privacy/custody constraints are accounted for.
